title: Light Sheet Microscopy
author: Clara Huesing
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wz3ff8n
materials: Open Impspector Pro software Must turn laser and microscope on before starting software (Version: Imspector Pro 328)
Within computer software, set instrument mode to CDC 2x (Figure 5) We use CDC2x because of the type of corrective cap that is attached to the front of the zoom objective Figure 5

steps.title: Prepare Cuvette and Mounting Apparatus
steps.instruction: Prepare the cuvette and position the mounting apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Remove the lid from the cuvette.

Handling only the frosted portion, place the cuvette onto the extended stage mounting apparatus and slowly lower it into position, ensuring the two frosted sides face the back and front of the microscope.
Fasten the metal coverpiece over the cuvette.

steps.title: Mount Tissue Sample
steps.instruction: Secure the tissue sample onto the mounting apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Gently push the sample onto the prongs of the metal piece ('hedgehog') inside the mounting apparatus, using minimal pressure to avoid damage.
Ensure the region of interest is facing upwards (e.g., ventral side up for sympathetic chain ganglia, or dorsal side up for intermediolateral bundle (IML) in the spinal cord).
Place the mounting apparatus into the cuvette.

steps.title: Configure Objective and Zoom
steps.instruction: Position the objective and set the magnification.

substeps.instruction: Position the objective piece over the cuvette; if using a Corrected lens, turn it to the halfway position.
Select the desired zoom factor on both the software program and the microscope knob (e.g., 0.63 for thoracic cavity overview images, or 2.0 or higher for individual sympathetic chain ganglia).

steps.title: Set Measurement and Laser Parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the system measurement parameters and initial laser settings.

substeps.instruction: Set measurement parameters (Xyz-Table Z, Ultrafilter, Xyz-Table X, Xyz-Table Y), ensuring all devices are 'on' and only 'ultrall filter' is checked.
Select the desired laser wavelengths based on fluorescent labeling and assign pseudocolors via the color gradient dropdown menu.
Set initial laser intensity to a low level (10%) to visualize tissue while minimizing photobleaching.

steps.title: Align Sample and Objective
steps.instruction: Bring the sample into the laser plane and submerge the objective.

substeps.instruction: Click the video icon to open the real-time view window.
Use the Z knob on the joystick to move the mounting apparatus up and down until the sample is in the plane of the lasers and optimally illuminated.
Use the coarse adjustment knob to lower the objective into the cuvette, monitoring the computer to ensure it submerges into the DBE without hitting the sample.
Use the X and Y joystick knobs to move the tissue left/right and forward/backward.
Continuously click the blue icon with the yellow star to adjust screen brightness during objective lowering.
Use the fine adjustment knob to sharpen the image, but avoid excessive time here until laser settings are customized.

steps.title: Optimize Laser and Chromatic Settings
steps.instruction: Fine-tune laser percentages and align multiple wavelengths.

substeps.instruction: Select the first laser to visualize and use the fine adjustment knob to create a crisp image; click 'Apply' to save settings.
If using multiple lasers, repeat the percentage setting and 'Apply' step for each laser.
Perform all coarse and fine adjustments on a single laser wavelength first.
To align other wavelengths, select the 'chromatic correction' button and use the arrow to bring the other lasers into focus.

steps.title: Define Z-Stack and Scan Range
steps.instruction: Set the imaging depth and step size in the 'Scan Range' window.

substeps.instruction: Rotate the Z-knob counterclockwise to the top of the tissue, click 'set as zero', and then click the compass button to define the 'start'.
Rotate the Z-knob clockwise to the bottom of the tissue and click the compass button to define the 'end'.
Determine the desired stepsize; the number of images will automatically populate, allowing for further adjustment of the stepsize.

steps.title: Execute Imaging
steps.instruction: Save settings and begin the scan.

substeps.instruction: Click 'autosave settings' on the left side of the screen to name and save the image.
In the 'Sample' window, select the liquid used in the cuvette (e.g., DBE) from the dropdown menu.
Click the 'play' button to begin the imaging process.
